messages:
lina: Quick sync — we're finalizing the on-prem metrics export handshake for Private customers. Need input on firewall rules, KMS key policy, and which telemetry fields to expose in the console. TL;DR: agent will push compressed protobuf batches to our collector over TLS, client cert-auth available for air-gapped setups.

sam: Nice — what exact ports/hosts should customers allow outbound? They always ask for an allowlist.

miguel: We'll use 443 to collector.redwood.internal (SNI-anchored). Fallback to collector-backup.redwood.internal. No plaintext HTTP. Agent will honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY envs.

lina: Agent config snippet we'll include in onboarding (dev copy):
```
# agent env example
REDWOOD_COLLECTOR=https://collector.redwood.example:443
REDWOOD_AGENT_ID=deployment-abc123
REDWOOD_KMS_KEY=projects/prod/keys/private-metrics
HTTP_PROXY=
HTTPS_PROXY=
# outbound allowlist: collector.redwood.example:443, collector-backup.redwood.example:443, s3.amazonaws.com:443 (optional backups)
```

sam: For customers that forbid internet egress, can we offer a PrivateLink/peering option so they don't need to open 443 to the public internet?

miguel: PrivateLink is on the roadmap but not ready. Short-term pattern: customer writes to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket in *their* account and we pull (cross-account role). That requires a KMS grant on their CMK or a shared key with proper grants. We'll document the exact IAM trust and kms:Decrypt/generateDataKey permissions.

annelie: Console/telemetry owners — what fields are must-have for dashboards (cost breakdown, latency, routing)? We need stable keys so we can index agent -> customer -> route.

lina: Minimal payload fields we plan to emit: customer_id, deployment_id, agent_version, batch_seq, batch_size, encoded_size_bytes, start_ts, end_ts, model_hint, route_policy (string e.g. "fallback_model_b"), and optional trace_id for correlation. Also include a boolean flag `kms_encrypted:true/false` to indicate CMK usage.

sam: On the KMS topic — customers will expect their CMKs (customer-managed). We should provide a snippet for the exact grant they must create. Example: they grant service account redwood-ingest@prod permission kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the CMK, plus an IAM role we can assume. Miguel, can audit-log hooks be toggled? Some compliance teams require we push audit events back into their logging account.

miguel: Yes, audit hooks are optional. Implementation: we publish audit events to a cross-account logs ingestion role (CloudWatch/Logging subscription). That needs an allowlist for our ingestion IPs and an STS AssumeRole trust policy. We'll include retention and redaction guidance in the security appendix.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: onboarding-agent-v2 pushed to staging at 1778904300 :rocket: (tests green)

annelie: UX ask: in the onboarding flow add a "Network & KMS checklist" section with: sample IP ranges, proxy env vars, exact KMS grant JSON, and a short flow diagram for the private S3 pull option. I'll draft a checklist and mock screenshots.

lina: I'll put together the full onboarding doc + checklist and drop a PR by EOD for review. Ping me if you want to co-author (cc @sam @miguel).

sam: +1, happy to review the KMS/IAM snippets.

miguel: I'll add the audit hook and assume-role examples.

annelie: thanks — this clarifies a lot. We'll want a short blurb in the console when a Private customer is onboarded explaining which export mode they chose and any manual steps.
